question: Does reinforcement learning optimization on lower-hop QA instances transfer effectively to higher-hop multi-hop queries, and what policy gradients or reward structures are most suitable?
description: Investigate existing RL transfer results in KGQA or related fields to gauge the plausibility of cross-hop policy transfer.
rationale: If transfer fails, the RL optimization stage may not contribute to the claimed improvement.
resolution: Existing work demonstrates RL transfer across question difficulty in KGQA: Temp-R1 uses reverse curriculum learning (training on hard questions first, transferring to easier ones) and achieves strong performance, showing that RL policies can generalize across hop complexity. Anticipation embedding and multi-perspective RL frameworks further indicate RL applicability to multi-hop KGQA. While direct evidence of training on lower-hop (easier) and transferring to higher-hop (harder) is not yet shown, the reverse curriculum result supports the feasibility of RL transfer across difficulty levels, suggesting the proposed lower-hop to higher-hop transfer is plausible.
